To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the market values the test weight and protein content, but not other quality characteristics, of exported wheat.
the market values test weight and protein content, but does not value moisture content, dockage, percentage of foreign matter, percentage of shranked and broken kernels, or grade.
only the test-weight and the protein-content characteristics used by the Federal Inspection Service to determine the grade of wheat are characteristics that influence price.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question whether the grain quality characteristics that are used to determine the grade of wheat are the characteristics that are valued by the market in determining the price of wheat exported by USA.
the market valuation of wheat grain quality factors.

the market valuation of the quality characteristics used by the Federal Inspection Service of the United States Department of Agriculture in the determination of the quality grades of the wheat exported by the United States.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the market does not value the quality factors used by FGIS in its grade determination.
test weight and protein content are the most important quality factors in determining the price of US wheat exported to the world market.
the market does value test weight and protein content but does not value the other quality characteristics used to determine the quality grade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the market valuation of the grain quality factors is not consistent and that the market valuation is not consistent with the valuation used by the Federal Government.

test weight and protein content are the only characteristics that consistently influence the export price of wheat, and that the price of wheat is more sensitive to changes in test weight than to changes in protein content.
the market valuation of wheat is consistent with the quality grades used by the Federal Government.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the market valuation of wheat characteristics is not uniform across the different types of wheat, nor is it uniform across the different countries.
the market does not value all quality characteristics equally.
the grain quality characteristics used to determine the grade of exported wheat are not the characteristics that the market uses to determine the price of the wheat.
